newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Gov. says economy strong, challenges remain.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Gov. says economy strong, challenges remain.

text.p: Washington's outgoing governor told lawmakers Tuesday the state economy was strong and its budget sound, but warned officials they would soon face fiscal challenges that could undermine future growth.

"Today, our state is in excellent shape," Gov. Mike Lowry said in his State of the State address. "Our economy is strong, our business climate has improved significantly, our commitments to education and the environment are intact."
Over the past four year, the state's umemployment rate has dropped from 8.4 percent to 5.8 percent. Its budget has gone from a $1.7 billion shortfall to a "healthy reserve," he said.
Despite these gains, Lowry warned lawmakers that the state was at a "crossroads."

"The challenge, over the coming months and years, is to continue that prosperity," Lowry said. "In the face of tighter budget constraints and even deeper cuts coming from the federal government, that task will not be simple."

Lowry said welfare reform and other cost-cutting measures approved by Congress would reduce state funding. Adjusting to the federal cutbacks and new state responsibilities would be "one of our greatest challenges," Lowry said.
"The worst of all possible solutions is for the state to act oblivious to those changes, make even deeper cuts, pass responsibility onto others and force people into the streets," the governor said.

"If we think that a few dollars a month in tax cuts for the average Washingtonian is more important than keeping food on the table for tens of thousands of low-income people in our state, we are a society in trouble," Lowry said.
He urged lawmakers to ensure that public schools keep pace with growth and warned that the state would suffer if its transportation system is neglected.
"We are, today, at a crossroads," Lowry said.

"One path divides us, denies the common good, and closes the door of prosperity to all but a few," he said. "The other path unites us, seeks the common good, and opens the door of opportunity to everyone."
